changelog: Replace E1 (hand-written example) with measured labeled example en_us_1567 so the scorer sees a real failure case where a very short trailing fragment (≤3 words) causes high entailment (contra) risk, addressing the primary finding.
findings: The scorer underestimates entailment (contra) risk for cuts that leave a very short trailing fragment. It treats locally-cohesive left/right translations as safe even when the right-hand fragment, taken alone, would assert/negate or mis‑scope a claim and so overturn the earlier material.

diagnosis.why: Replacing E1 with a real short trailing-fragment example made the scorer avoid keeping tiny trailing fragments (small positive changes in the ≤3 and ≤5 bins), but the model compensated by introducing more internal single-word splits and moving cuts closer to heads in longer pieces (negative changes in ≤7, ≤10, ≤99). The worst-moved pairs illustrate this side-effect (new one-word segments like “they”, “medication”, “upright”).
diagnosis.lesson: When adding an example to discourage very-short trailing fragments, ensure the change is localized so it does not induce extra internal one-word splits or shift cuts toward heads in longer pieces.
